events.title: Liberation of Dachau Concentration Camp
events.description: United States Seventh Army troops, including soldiers of the 45th Infantry Division and 42nd Infantry Division, liberated the Dachau concentration camp in Germany, finding thousands of survivors and many corpses in railway cars.
events.significance: The liberation exposed the horrors of the Nazi concentration camp system to the world and provided crucial evidence of the Holocaust.

events.title: Adolf Hitler Marries Eva Braun and Dictates His Will
events.description: In the Führerbunker in Berlin, as Soviet forces closed in, Hitler married Eva Braun and dictated his last will and political testament. He died by suicide the following day.
events.significance: These events marked the final hours of the Nazi regime and the imminent end of World War II in Europe.

events.title: Los Angeles Riots Begin
events.description: Riots erupted in Los Angeles after a jury acquitted four police officers of charges in the beating of Rodney King. Six days of unrest resulted in more than 60 deaths and about $1 billion in property damage.
events.significance: The riots highlighted deep racial tensions, police brutality, and economic inequality in the United States and prompted national debate and reforms.

events.title: Death of Alfred Hitchcock
events.description: Sir Alfred Hitchcock, the English film director known as the Master of Suspense, died in Los Angeles at age 80. His films included Psycho, Vertigo, North by Northwest, and Rear Window.
events.significance: Hitchcock revolutionized the thriller genre and film techniques, and his influence on cinema continues today.

events.title: James Cook Lands at Botany Bay
events.description: Captain James Cook and the crew of HMS Endeavour made their first landing on the eastern coast of Australia at a place he later named Botany Bay.
events.significance: The landing led to British claims on eastern Australia and eventually to the colonization of the continent, profoundly affecting Indigenous Australians.
